rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Poetry's contrivance is far from prophetic nature; it is used for praise and blame and is mostly false, making it unfitting for the noblest prophet.
rows.anchor: فكيف بأشرفهم مما يكتسب به مدحا وهجوا , فيكون أكثره كذبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here, what is not fitting means what is neither proper nor sought nor possible for him, given his rank and high aspiration.
rows.anchor: أي وما يصح ولا ينطلب ولا يتأتى أصلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Poetry deliberately follows a set meter and rhyme; those constraints force inversions and circumlocutions that obscure meaning and make it hard to understand.
rows.anchor: أن الشعر - وهو تعمد صوغ الكلام على وزن معلوم وقافية ملتزمة - نقيصة

words: إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا ذِكْرٌۭ وَقُرْءَانٌۭ مُّبِينٌۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The revelation is an honor and admonition, gathers wisdom for this life and the next, is recited in prayer, and brings success in both abodes through recitation and practice.
rows.anchor: أي شرف وموعظة { وقرآن } أي جامع للحكم كلها دنيا وأخرى يتلى في المحاريب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an makes its contents manifest to anyone who truly seeks them, whether clever or dull; poetry, despite its lesser eloquence, admonishes only the very intelligent.
rows.anchor: بعد أن يشترط في مطلق فهمه ومجرد اللذة به الذكي والغبي والحديد والبليد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ending of Sād clarifies that the Qur'an is a reminder for all people, clever and dull alike, whereas poetry is for the exceptionally intelligent.
rows.anchor: ويبين هذا المعنى غاية البيان آخر ( ص )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose is for the Messenger to warn; the clear Qur'an has formed him, so he manifests it and his state calls every truly living person to believe.
rows.anchor: وكان الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم متخلقا به

rows.speaker: نافع وابن عامر ويعقوب
rows.claim: These authorities read the verb with direct address, 'so that you warn'; al-Biqāʿī takes this as indicating that no one understands the Qur'an fully as the Prophet does.
rows.anchor: ويؤيده لفت الكلام في قراءة نافع وابن عامر ويعقوب بالخطاب إشارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The living person is one with complete inward life that leads to everlasting life; such a person is in truth a believer even if outward signs initially suggest otherwise.
rows.anchor: كونا متمكنا { حيا } أي حياة كاملة معنوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular for the living follows the word's grammatical form and hints at the few fortunate; the plural for disbelievers follows its meaning and signals the many wretched.
rows.anchor: وأفرد الضمير هنا على اللفظ إشارة إلى قلة السعداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word that becomes binding is punishment, and the disbelievers are those deeply rooted in disbelief, dead in reality though they appear alive.
rows.anchor: أي يجب ويثبت { القول } أي بالعذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse uses ellipsis by reciprocal implication: faith is omitted from the first clause because its opposite appears in the second, and death is omitted from the second because its opposite appears in the first.
rows.anchor: فالآية من الاحتباك : حذف الإيمان أولا لما دل عليه من ضده ثانيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an's governing aim is serious meaning, with words following it; poets and rhymers put rhyme and cadence first, which can produce weak or false meanings.
rows.anchor: أن أعظم منافاة القرآن للشعر وكذا السجع من أجل أنه جد كله

rows.speaker: حسان بن ثابت
rows.claim: At the expedition of al-Ghāba, Ḥassān's rhyming verse angered Saʿd ibn Zayd al-Ashhalī, who gave his horses to al-Miqdād and swore not to speak to him; Ḥassān explained the rhyme had forced the name.
rows.anchor: قال حسان بن ثابت رضي الله عنه وحاله معروف في البلاغة والتفنن في أساليب الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet never chooses wording merely for polish or meter; he avoids a metrical option when it fails to convey the intended meaning, just as Arabs avoid grammatical error because it is error.
rows.anchor: فالنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يدور في فكره أبدا قصد اللفظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular is kept for the speaker because the account concerns the saved man's rebuke and self-congratulation; a plural would wrongly suggest that everyone spoke, so his words can instruct the reader.
rows.anchor: لم يجمع الضمير لئلا يلبس فيوهم أنه للجميع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The middle of Hell is called its sawāʾ because it is equidistant from the surrounding sides, like the center of a circle.
rows.anchor: وسمي الوسط سواء لاستواء المسافة منه إلى الجوانب كمركز الدائرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath and emphatic wording stress how the companion's words had often affected the speaker through Satan's embellishment of desire and relief from religious duties.
rows.anchor: أكد قوله إشارة إلى أنه كان يؤثر فيه قوله في كثير من الأوقات بما يزينه به الشيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The companion had nearly ruined him and brought him to the worst of places; the emphases also express surprise that he escaped such influence.
rows.anchor: أي إنك قاربت أن تهلكني وتجعلني في أردأ ما يكون من الأماكن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The strong emphasis urges anyone close to wavering to remain firm and to keep away from evil companions.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا التأكيد غاية الترغيب في الثبات لمن كان قريبا من التزلزل وفي المباعدة لقرناء السوء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He attributes his rescue to his Lord's kindness: God raised him to resist following the companion and overlooked his association with him.
rows.anchor: أي المحسن إلي بما رباني به من تثبيتي عن أتباعك والتجاوز عني في مخالطتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without that grace he would have been compelled to attend the cramped, painful place where his companion is; seeing the former tormentor there also warns against bad company.
rows.anchor: أي المكرهين على حضور هذا الموطن الضنك الذي أنت فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Overcome by sudden joy, the speaker asks his companions whether they will die or be punished, then stresses that they will experience only their first death and calls their state a great victory.
rows.anchor: أي أنحن يا إخواني منعمون مخلدون فيتسبب عن ذلك أنا ما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People should work for this reward: it gives lasting abundance with no later poverty, unlike worldly things for which people compete, which quickly vanish and bring weariness.
rows.anchor: أي الجزاء { فليعمل العاملون * } أي لينالوه فإنهم يغتنون غنى لا فقر بعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bliss described is only a small initial welcome for a guest, compared with what lies beyond human comprehension.
rows.anchor: فأشار بذلك إلى أنه إنما هو شيء يسير كما يقدم للضيف عند نزوله على ما لاح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zaqqum is known for foulness and bitterness; the word evokes consuming food reluctantly and with great difficulty.
rows.anchor: أي التي تعرفها بأنها في غاية النتن والمرارة

words: أَذَٰلِكَ خَيْرٌ نُّزُلًا أَمْ شَجَرَةُ ٱلزَّقُّومِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The incomparable alternatives are deliberately balanced to expose the unbelievers' bad choice: they treated the deeds leading to punishment as better than believers' deeds and so deserve this rebuke.
rows.anchor: وعادل بين ما لا معادلة بينهما بوجه تنبيها على ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God utterly destroyed the rest of Lot's people, clearing the holy region of them and their evil deeds without sparing anyone or needing another's permission.
rows.anchor: فجردنا الأرض من قاذوراتهم ونزهنا البلاد المقدسة منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh merchants passed the sites of Lot's towns, identified with the Dead Sea, on their Syria trade, in the morning and at night; the morning recalls when those towns were destroyed.
rows.anchor: وكان تجار قريش يرون البقعة التي كانت فيها أماكن قوم لوط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lot's people's fate should make rational people fear the same end and believe their Messenger; Quraysh are even more liable to punishment because their own people know their Prophet's noble lineage, speech, and conduct.
rows.anchor: فإنكم أجدر منهم بالأخذ لأنه منكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After accounts of peoples destroyed in this life or the next, the narrative turns to Jonah, whose people ended in safety, faith, and blessing, favoring hope alongside consolation.
rows.anchor: ختم بمن آل أمر قومه إلى سلامة وإيمان ونعمة وإحسان تغليبا للترجية على التأسية

rows.speaker: البغوي
rows.claim: Al-Baghawī relates that Elijah hid from the threatened king at Baalbek; he later prayed for the dead infant Jonah at the mother's pleading, and God restored the child after fourteen days.
rows.anchor: حكى البغوي في قصة إلياس عليه السلام أنه لما أرسله الله تعالى إلى سبطه من بني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jonah's story consoles the Prophet over the Quraysh's arrogance: it shows the difficulty and burden of messengership and God's special care for messengers, chosen with knowledge and not abandoned despite their efforts to flee their charge.
rows.anchor: ذكر من أمر يونس عيله السلام ما يعرف منه صعوبة أمر الرسالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abaqa means to flee from one's master to a place where he thinks he will be hidden; Jonah fled from the Master who had honored him with prophethood, out of weakness in bearing the mission.
rows.anchor: أي هرب حين أرسل من سيده الذي تشرفه الله بالرسالة ضعفا عن حملها لأن الاباق الهرب من السيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fulk is a vessel traveling on the sea, and mashḥūn means fully loaded with no room for anything else; its immediate departure implies there was no reason for the crew to wait.
rows.anchor: أي البيت الذي يسافر فيه على ظهر البحر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: As cited by al-Kirmānī and others, people of the sea held that a ship would not sail steadily while carrying a fugitive slave; the storm led the crew to cast lots.
rows.anchor: نقله الكرماني وغيره عن ابن عباس رضي الله الله عنهما

rows.speaker: البغوي
rows.claim: Al-Baghawī explains musāhama as casting arrows to draw lots; Jonah cast lots with the crew, in keeping with their custom in such a crisis.
rows.anchor: قال البغوي : والمساهمة إلقاء السهام على جهة القرعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word evokes slipping on a slippery place: the lot made Jonah fall from his high position into the sea when the crew threw him overboard.
rows.anchor: عبر عن ذلك بما يدل على الزلق الذي يكون من علو إلى سفل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The whale gulped Jonah as one swallows a morsel; it is the familiar, largest whale, phrased as though there were no other whale.
rows.anchor: أي ابتلعه كما تبتلع اللقمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mulīm describes Jonah as entering a state that calls for blame.
rows.anchor: أي داخل في الملامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the crisis Jonah became detached from himself and all else, abiding in the oneness of God through glorification; this inward state points to why God saved him.
rows.anchor: فتجرد عن نفسه وغيرها تجردا لم يكن لأحد مثل مجموعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jonah was innately and habitually given to glorifying God with heart, tongue, and limbs, including prayer, in both ease and hardship because his character matched his created purpose.
rows.anchor: وهو ما يصح إطلاق التسبيح في اللغة عليه من التنزيه بالقلب واللسان والأركان بالصلاة وغيرها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets Jonah's being among those who glorify God as referring to prayer.
rows.anchor: وحمله ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما على الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without his prior glorification Jonah would have remained alive in the fish, or else become its food and have his parts mixed with it.
rows.anchor: أي حيا أو بأن يكون غذاء له فتختلط أجزاؤه بأجزائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural ending conveys resurrection of all creatures: a singular could exclude animals, while a dual could imply that only Jonah and the fish rise.
rows.anchor: وعبر بالجمع لإفادة عموم البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage alludes to the saying about knowing God in ease so He will know one in hardship, and urges remembrance while magnifying its importance.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية إشارة إلى حديث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because Jonah remembered God in ease, God remembered and rescued him in hardship; the rescue was an astonishing act of divine greatness.
rows.anchor: ولكنه لما كان ذكارا لله في حال الرخاء ذكرناه في حال الشدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿarāʾ is a broad, empty, barren place with no shelter or vegetation; al-Biqāʿī locates it on the coast of Mosul.
rows.anchor: أي المكان القفر الواسع الخالي عن ساتر عن نبت أو غيره

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān gives the location where the fish cast Jonah as Naṣībīn in the region of Mosul.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حيان : قذفه في نصيبين من ناحية الموصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jonah was gravely ill, like a newborn, but by God's rescuing grace he was not blameworthy and was among the chosen and righteous.
rows.anchor: عليل مما ناله من جوف الحوت بحيث أنه كام كالطفل ساعة يولد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural of majesty emphasizes God's power to bring forth vegetation even in a place with no natural conditions for growth.
rows.anchor: في ذلك المكان لا مقتضى للنبات مطلقا فيه فضلا عما لا ينبت إلا بالماء الكثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plant was raised above Jonah to shade him as a house shades a person.
rows.anchor: ورفعناها حال إنباتنا إياها فوقه لتظله كما يظل البيت الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yaqṭīn is a plant that spreads along the ground, does not survive winter, and has no trunk, such as melon and cucumber; calling it a tree highlights its unusual growth.
rows.anchor: كل ما يمتد وينبسط على وجه الأرض ولا يبقى على الشتاء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the plant as a gourd, valued for its large leaves, cool shade, soft texture, and repelling flies.
rows.anchor: كما قاله ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما شجرة القرع لعظم ورقها وبرد ظلها

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says that sprinkling water from the gourd's leaves on a place keeps flies away entirely.
rows.anchor: قال أبو حيان : وماء ورقه إذا رش به مكان لا يقربه ذباب أصلا

rows.speaker: غيره
rows.claim: Another authority says gourd rind suits the human body: placed over a missing piece of skull, it lets flesh grow and fill the gap.
rows.anchor: وقال غيره : فيه ملاءمة لجسد الإنسان حتى لو ذهبت عظمة من رأسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The term is linked to q-ṭ-n, dwelling in a place for a temporary rather than permanent stay, like the plant's nature.
rows.anchor: وهو من قطن بالمكان - إذا أقام به إقامة زائل لا ثابت

rows.speaker: مترجمه
rows.claim: The translator's Book of Jonah recounts Jonah's commission to Nineveh and flight by ship, a storm and lot that identify him, his being thrown overboard and swallowed by a great fish, and his prayer after three days and nights in its belly.
rows.anchor: قال مترجمه : نبدأ بمعونة الله وقوته بكتب نبوة يونان بن متى النبي

rows.speaker: مترجمه
rows.claim: Jonah is recommissioned; Nineveh fasts, repents, and is spared, while he resents the mercy, shelters under a gourd destroyed by a worm, and God asks why he pities it but not the vast city.
rows.anchor: فأمر الرب السمكة فقذفت يونان في اليبس , وأتى الكلام الرب إليه المرة الثانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He suggests the gourd began growing when Jonah emerged from the fish; on returning later, it had grown enough for him to build a shelter, reconciling the account with historians' reports.
rows.anchor: ولعل أصل القرع المذكور هنا كان نبت عليه حين خرج من بطن الحوت
